body: SME IPOs boomed in FY24 and FY25: the RBI noted a strong surge driven by retail participation, and the BSE SME IPO index outperformed the mainboard IPO index and the Sensex. Symbol of the mania (from memory, not re-verified here): Resourceful Automobile (Aug 2024), a Delhi two-wheeler dealer with two showrooms and a handful of employees, raised ~Rs 12 crore and was oversubscribed ~400x; many SME issues were subscribed hundreds of times. SEBI officials warned in 2024 of manipulation, inflated financials and 'pump and dump' in SME listings; NSE capped SME listing-day gains at 90% (2024, from memory). SEBI board on 18 Dec 2024 tightened norms (in ICDR by Mar 2025): minimum EBITDA of Rs 1 crore in 2 of 3 years, minimum application of two lots, and other limits; exchanges applied new SME rules from 1 July 2025; by May 2025 some SME IPOs excluded retail bids under Rs 2 lakh. In Oct 2026 a SEBI working group/consultation proposed a further overhaul (e.g., scrapping compulsory 3-year market making). Post-listing, many 2024 SME stocks fell sharply in 2025 (no index-level figure found; unverified). Signals at the top: absurd subscription multiples for tiny, unknown issuers, listing pops used as the investment case, promoter-linked merchant bankers, regulator warnings. Lesson: same as the 1990s IPO boom - when the quality of what is being listed collapses, expect the worst losses there first.

data.policy: SEBI 18 Dec 2024; exchange rules 1 Jul 2025; Oct 2026 review
data.signals: 100-1000x subscription for tiny issuers; regulator warnings

title: 2024 SME IPO mania and SEBI's clampdown
